statement: Public-corpus propositions where this port follows the pinned Java oracle over an RFC-strict reading, with the ledger record that discloses each one. It exists because the reserved-bit ready-state divergence was found by a cross-plane audit reading another plane's manifest by hand, and no gate of ours would have found it — nor the eighteen sibling instances the same mechanism produces. Rows are swept mechanically from committed evidence (the public corpus and the live pinned-Java transcript), never from another plane's artifacts: this census is deliberately independent of the Codex plane's evidence/oracle-hierarchy.json, so the two planes' normative choices stay separately auditable. Every row must carry a ledger_delta_id that resolves in evidence/java/behavior-delta-ledger.json, and internal/deltaledger enforces that, so a newly observed divergence refuses the gate until it is ledgered.
completeness: The protocol-rejection-readystate class is COMPLETE over the 74-scenario public tier by the stated predicate, and internal/deltaledger re-derives it from the corpus on every run, so a new scenario that falls in the class fails the suite until it is enrolled here. Completeness is claimed for THAT CLASS ONLY. Other Java-over-RFC propositions exist in the corpus (consumed-byte rejection sites, error-site offsets, the absent automatic pong) and are disclosed in the ledger, but they are not swept by a mechanical predicate and this census does not claim to enumerate them.

entries.derivation: MECHANICAL SWEEP of corpora/public/scenarios.jsonl: outcome==error AND error.close_code in {1002,1007,1009} AND final_state=='open'. Complete over the 74-scenario public tier by that predicate.
entries.rfc_strict_expectation: closed — RFC 6455 section 7.1.7 requires Failing the WebSocket Connection on this error, which takes the endpoint out of OPEN
entries.java_entry_point_note: NOT a clean RFC-versus-Java split. Shipped WebSocketImpl.decodeFrames DOES close on this rejection (its InvalidDataException arm calls close(e) at WebSocketImpl.java:404-407). The oracle adapter never routes through decodeFrames — it calls draft.translateFrame directly (OracleEngine.java:343) and uses WebSocketImpl only as the processFrame listener (OracleEngine.java:387) — so the close ladder is unreachable and the ready state stays open. Both readings are Java-faithful; they are faithful to different entry points of the same pinned runtime.
